items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

`MultiTeacherModelManager` used to build one `TeacherModelManager` per teacher in a plain `for` loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully up. With N teachers the wall clock was N x (engine init + CUDA graph capture). Teachers run on disjoint devices and share nothing, so this serialization was pure latency.

items.title: [Perf] disaggregation: Send replicated KV heads from one prefill rank
items.author: Denji-kk
items.summary: When a model has fewer KV heads than the prefill attention TP size, several prefill ranks hold an identical copy of the same head. In the Mooncake heterogeneous-TP path every one of those ranks writes its copy into the same decode buffer.
items.body:
## Motivation

When a model has fewer KV heads than the prefill attention TP size, several prefill ranks hold an identical copy of the same head. In the Mooncake heterogeneous-TP path every one of those ranks writes its copy into the same decode buffer. With one KV head and prefill attention TP8 → decode TP1, each decode rank receives 8x the logical KV bytes. The slice path also posts one RDMA descriptor per token slot, so long prompts pay for both the duplicate writes and the descriptor count.

## Modifications

- `should_send_kv_replica` in `disaggregation/common/utils.py` elects one writer

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail a dead peer's sibling ports on the same host at once (opt-in)
items.author: sohom-cs
items.summary: Adds opt-in `group_peers_by_host` grouping so a dead P2P rank's sibling sessions on the same host are reaped together, preventing continued load to a degraded node.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes 1 and 3 of #56828.

A P2P peer is identified by `host:port` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py:128-133`), and each DP rank binds its own port (`manager.py:344-348`). So a source pod with 8 DP ranks is 8 unrelated sessions on the consumer. When one rank's session dies, `_reap_dead_sessions` reaps only that `peer_id` (`manager.py:872`, `:878`). The sessions to the pod's other ranks stay up, and so do their loads.

With the new P2P tier option `group_peers_by_host`, a dead peer also takes down the sessions to the other ports on its host, and that host gets no new out

items.title: [Perf][Parser] Skip tool-argument conversions after a replaced value
items.author: vMaroon
items.summary: When a tool call repeats a key whose value was already streamed, fails the prefix check before it installs the argument value extender. Every later delta then re-converts the whole argument text, only to fail the same check, so the API server's cost per token …
items.body:
## Overview

When a tool call repeats a key whose value was already streamed, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` fails the prefix check before it installs the argument value extender. Every later delta then re-converts the whole argument text, only to fail the same check, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call. This installs the extender with streaming off on that failure. Follow-up to #61253 and #64535.

## Claims

- On GLM-4.7/GLM-5.x, a long value written under a repeated key costs 15.1 us per engine step at 66K output chars, against 2514 us on main. From 64K to 256K chars

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Serve SageMaker /ping and mark /invocations unsupported
items.author: hemuku90
items.summary: Fixes Rust frontend returning 404 for /ping and /invocations routes by mirroring Python frontend behavior, enabling SageMaker health-check compatibility.
items.body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend returns a bare 404 for `/ping` and `/invocations`. The Python frontend always registers both for SageMaker (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/api_router.py`), and SageMaker health-checks a container through `/ping`, so a SageMaker deployment with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` never comes up healthy.

This serves `GET`/`POST /ping` with the existing `/health` handler, which is what Python does and what the Rust render server already does (`routes/render.rs`). `/invocations` gets the standard 501 placeholder the router uses for other Python routes it doesn't implement

items.summary: On SM90, DeepSeek-V4.1 decode scores each query row against its whole visible compressed context with. The grid gives every row a fixed CTAs, which scan the row's tiles serially, so a single long request sets the kernel time while most SMs are idle.
items.body:
## Motivation

On SM90, DeepSeek-V4.1 decode scores each query row against its whole visible compressed context with `fp4_index_logits_paged`. The grid gives every row a fixed `min(cdiv(max_len, 64), cdiv(num_sms * 4, rows))` CTAs, which scan the row's tiles serially, so a single long request sets the kernel time while most SMs are idle. Under DP attention every rank waits for the slowest one, so one long context slows every request on the node.

## Modifications

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

LiquidAI released LFM3 on 2026-10-27: LFM3-1.7B (text), LFM3-VL-2B, LFM3-Audio-2B, LFM3-Omni-2B and the d1 models. vLLM has no `Lfm3ForCausalLM`.

items.title: [None][fix] Reject variable-width beam search under overlap
items.author: jongukc
items.summary: With the overlap scheduler, two concurrent requests whose widens (for example ) can read KV that no forward wrote. To keep the batch width uniform, the scheduler skips one request for an iteration while its generation position still advances.
items.body:
Under the overlap scheduler, concurrent requests that widen through beam_width_array can be skipped for one iteration to keep the batch width uniform while their generation position still advances. Their next attention step then reads a KV position that no forward wrote. Reject a changing beam_width_array at request validation when overlap is enabled; constant arrays and disable_overlap_scheduler=True are unaffected. Document the restriction.

items.body:
## Motivation

Add [Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex](https://huggingface.co/Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex) to SGLang Diffusion.

Pika H3 Flex is not a new checkpoint. It is MiniMax-H3 plus two FP32 LoRA adapters (rank/alpha 128): `fl2va` covers t2va/fl2va and `ref2va` covers ref2va. The adapters were post-trained for a fixed six-step sampler:

- knots `1000/750/500/250/100/40`, shifted per modality (video 12, audio 3)
- a re-noising update: predict x0, then re-noise to the next sigma with fresh noise

`--model-path Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex` serves t2va/fl2va, and `--model-variant ref2va` serves ref2va.

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Summary

Add an opt-in FlyDSL MoE backend for ROCm gfx942, using [ROCm/aiter#6995](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6995). items.title: Reject GTP weight remat in Megatron-FSDP v1
items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: Adds a validation check to Megatron-FSDP v1 that raises ValueError when GTP weight rematerialization is enabled, preventing incorrect parameter sharding and opaque mesh-construction errors.
items.body:
**Why.** GTP weight rematerialization gives each rank of a GTP group a different shard of a weight, and only Megatron DDP handles it. Megatron-FSDP v1 shards and reduces parameters over one data-parallel group with no GTP handling, so neither group it can pick is correct:
- Without a `pg_collection`, the adapter takes the GTP-inclusive group from `parallel_state`. Construction succeeds, and FSDP shards and reduces across ranks that hold different GTP shards as if they were replicas.
- With the grid's collection, it takes the replicate `dp_cp`, and mesh construction fails with an opaque einops

items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: Passes the process group collection to SequentialMLP experts so their fc1/fc2 linears use local shard/replica groups instead of global parallel state.

**Why.** `SequentialMLP` builds each local expert `MLP` with only `tp_group=expt_tp` and no collection. The expert `fc1` and `fc2` then:
- resolve their GTP-remat group through `resolve_gtp_remat_group(None, is_expert=True)`, which reads the global `expt_gtp_remat`;
- stamp no replica group on their GTP shards, so checkpointing elects the shard writer from `parallel_state.get_expert_data_parallel_rank()`.

A model on its own grid gets its experts sharded over the global group, or left unsharded when the globals do not exist, and reads the global grid to save them. `TEGroupedMLP` already passes

## Motivation

The AMD CI AITER check never rebuilds AITER when the Dockerfile pin is bumped. The image reports a pip version like `v0.1.26.dev144+g285579b62.d20261027`, which never equals the full commit in `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`. The next check (`dev` or `+g<hash>`) always matches, so the script prints "Dev/patched version detected → skipping rebuild".

This matters because jobs often run on an image that predates the pin bump: ARC runners start with a preloaded image about a day old, and PR jobs prefer cached images. Those jobs then test the image's old AITER instead of the pinned one. Nigh

items.title: [Bugfix][SleepMode] Exact-size, reusable pinned CPU backup for level-1 sleep
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Eliminates ~2x host memory overhead in level-1 sleep by replacing torch's CachingHostAllocator-padded pinned buffers with exact-size reusable CPU backup tensors.
items.body:
## Problem

Level-1 sleep backs up every cumem allocation to host memory with `torch.empty(size, pin_memory=True)`. torch's `CachingHostAllocator` rounds each pinned block up to a power of two and keeps freed blocks in its cache, so the level-1 backup costs up to ~2x the offloaded bytes in host memory, and that memory is never returned to the OS. On Mistral Large 4 at TP8 the backup is 85.19 GiB per GPU, which turned into roughly +578 GiB of host memory per node.

## Root cause

The backup size is chosen by the caching host allocator, not by the allocation. The old code already kept the memory

items.title: [Multimodal] Cache PyNvVideoCodec decoder caps
items.author: brandonpelfrey
items.summary: The PyNvVideoCodec (NVDEC) video backend calls on every request, from. Each call takes ~180 ms and holds the GIL, so it freezes the whole API server process for that long. [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Overview

The PyNvVideoCodec (NVDEC) video backend calls `nvc.GetDecoderCaps` on every request, from `PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackendMixin._validate_decoder_caps`. Each call takes ~180 ms and holds the GIL, so it freezes the whole API server process for that long. The result only depends on the device, codec, chroma format and bit depth, so this PR caches it in a bounded LRU (64 entries).

## Claims

- **Removes ~185 ms of fixed cost from every NVDEC video request.** The caps check drops from 183–190 ms to 0.3–1.6 ms. It also removes the ~180 ms freeze of the API server's event loop per reques

## Purpose

**Stacked on #63416 (NIXL pairs KV regions by layer) and #64109 (DFlash/DSpark drafter KV backs only its tail).** The branch merges both. Only the last three commits are this PR; the rest is theirs.

This PR adds `--draft-kv-pool`, which gives a DFlash or DSpark drafter's sliding-window KV its own block pool.

With the hybrid KV cache manager every group draws from one pool, and every block is as large as the widest group's. A drafter group of a few sliding-window layers therefore pays a target-sized block for each of its blocks. RFC #59117 measures what this costs on a GDN target

items.title: [Fix] model_loader: Neutral UE8M0 block scales for dummy weights
items.author: wwl2755
items.summary: Fixes dummy-weight initialization for MXFP8 layers by setting UE8M0 block scales to neutral value 127 instead of zero, preventing near-zero outputs and downstream NaN propagation.
items.body:
## Motivation

`initialize_dummy_weights` only initializes floating-point tensors. MXFP8 layers allocate their UE8M0 block scales (`weight_scale_inv`) as `torch.uint8` zeros (`fp8.py`, MoE and linear `create_weights`), so with `--load-format dummy` those scales stay 0. In UE8M0, 0 means 2^-127, so every MXFP8 weight dequantizes to roughly zero. The MXFP8 layers then produce near-zero outputs, which can propagate to NaN downstream.

## Modifications

- `initialize_dummy_weights`: fill uint8 `*weight_scale_inv` tensors with 127 (2^0), the UE8M0 counterpart of the existing neutral FP4 global scal

items.author: KrishnanPrash

## Overview

Adds `MediaItem.nixl_ref` to the vllm-rs gRPC API: a client that already decoded an image sends a NIXL descriptor of its pixels, and vllm-rs reads them with a one-sided NIXL READ instead of decoding the file again. Each turn of a computer-use agent re-sends its screenshot history, and vllm-rs decodes every screenshot again on the request path, even when the prefix cache holds its KV. Opt-in: cargo feature `nixl-media` and `--enable-grpc-nixl-media`.

items.author: zhongdaor-nv
items.summary: The gRPC server hands a plain to tonic through. tonic applies its setting only to listeners it binds itself, so the sockets this server accepts keep Nagle's algorithm enabled.

## Motivation

The `runtime.v1` gRPC server (`rust/sglang-grpc`) hands a plain `TcpListener` to tonic through

sockets this server accepts keep Nagle's algorithm enabled. Streamed responses are one small frame per token, all
flowing server → client with almost nothing coming back, which is exactly the pattern where Nagle plus the client's
delayed ACK stalls the sender: each frame waits for the previous one to be acknowledged, and the acknowledgement is

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.author: micah-wil
items.summary: Skips AITER tuned GEMM and falls back to hipBLASLt on gfx950 when M*N >= 2^31, working around an int32 output-offset overflow that crashes large encoder models like MiniMax-M3-MXFP4.
items.body:
## Overview

items.title: [Perf] [AMD] mooncake: pack heterogeneous-TP SWA KV pages
items.author: Lzy17
items.summary: Optimizes Mooncake KV cache packing by gathering destination-local SWA heads and writing whole pages directly when prefill and decode TP sizes differ, cutting TTFT ~2x on MI355X.
items.body:
## Motivation

With prefill TP smaller than decode TP, Mooncake still sends SWA head slices as many small ranges, even when full KV uses staging.

## Modifications

Add default-off `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_SWA_PACKING`: gather destination-local heads and write whole pages directly into the final SWA pool. Validate NHD/GQA geometry and page bounds; unsupported peers fall back before submission. Registered scratch defaults to 64 MiB per initialized worker. Uncertain completion quarantines buffers. Existing full-KV staging and native Mooncake are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

15 CPU tests pass

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Don't count a retried store offer toward store_threshold
items.author: sohom-cs
items.summary: With, admits a chunk to the CPU tier only after it has been offered that many times. When can't allocate, it returns, and the offloading scheduler offers the same keys again on a later step.
items.body:
## Overview

With `store_threshold >= 2`, `CPUOffloadingManager` admits a chunk to the CPU tier only after it has been offered that many times. When `prepare_store()` can't allocate, it returns `None`, and the offloading scheduler offers the same keys again on a later step. Each retry counted as another offer, so a chunk that only one request ever had could be admitted by that request's own retry. With this PR, a retry of a failed offer doesn't count again.

## Claims

- When a request offers the keys of its failed `prepare_store()` call again, the retry doesn't add to their counts.

items.body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.2 with DP attention runs the triton sparse-MLA decode with all 64 heads on each rank, an fp8 KV cache, and topk 2048. MTP adds 6 verify rows per request. This PR adds a decode plan for that shape:
- **Speed.** The kernel is 2.4x to 3.2x faster at 48 to 96 rows.
- **Accuracy.** It is within fp8 tolerance of an fp32 reference: 37 to 38 dB SNR, against 26 to 37 dB on main.

## Motivation

DFLASH V2 manually constructs the draft `ForwardBatch` instead of using the normal scheduler-to-forward-batch initialization path. As a result, the draft batch did not inherit the scheduler's CUDA-graph eligibility votes or initialize the token-count metadata used by TP/DP synchronization.

The draft graphs were captured successfully at server startup, but runtime draft steps retained the default graph state and executed eagerly. Profiles showed roughly 100 individual kernel launches per draft step and no `hipGraphLaunch`, while target verification replayed its graph normally.

items.title: [Fix] quantization: Preserve CT MoE zero-point channel order
items.author: nickmatteo
items.summary: Asymmetric MoE zero points are stored in natural output-channel order. The Marlin postload path currently sends those words through, which undoes AWQ's extra input interleave.
items.body:
## Motivation

Asymmetric `pack-quantized` MoE zero points are stored in natural output-channel order. The Marlin postload path currently sends those words through `moe_awq_to_marlin_zero_points`, which undoes AWQ's extra input interleave. This changes which zero point belongs to each CT output channel and produces incorrect expert outputs when the zero points vary across channels.

## Modifications

Convert each expert's CT zero points with `unpack_cols` followed directly by `marlin_zero_points`, matching the existing dense CT path. Apply the conversion to both gate/up and down projections.

items.author: mmdbhs
items.summary: In EPD mode, an Encoder request can fail before multimodal input IDs have been generated. For example, may return HTTP 502 when the Encoder connection is reset.

## Motivation

In EPD mode, an Encoder request can fail before multimodal input IDs have been generated. For example, `/scheduler_receive_meta_data` may return HTTP 502 when the Encoder connection is reset.

While streaming the error response, `OutputStreamer` calls `len(req.origin_input_ids)`, raising a `TypeError` and causing the scheduler process to exit. items.title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: Speed up the gfx950 swap-AB decode attention
items.author: anhminhnguyenhoang
items.summary: On gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4 decode with at most 8 query rows runs. One call takes 12 to 14 µs. [Discussion: db79d2c21a folds the three gfx950 test files into, with every case kept.]
items.body:
## Motivation

On gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4 decode with at most 8 query rows runs `swapab_attention`. One call takes 12 to 14 µs. Its grid has 2 to 60 programs on 256 CUs, so the latency of one program sets the call time. A sparse call at bs 4 reads about 1.5 MB, under 3% of the 8.0 TB/s HBM peak.

The partial kernel spends that latency on the KV page load, on LDS round trips for the KV tile, P, and the epilogue, and on 16x16x16 MFMAs. The combine waits on loads it can issue early, and it rotates tiles that hold no rope dims. After these changes, swap-AB is also faster than the aiter route
discussion: db79d2c21a folds the three gfx950 test files into `test_swapab_attention.py`, with every case kept. On MI355X: 15 passed, 2 skipped (the SM100-only cases).

items.body:
## Purpose

The Mooncake P2P KV connector reaches the Transfer Engine directly: the worker creates the engine, registers memory, submits one synchronous batch per request and reads back a single status. That leaves no place to choose another engine and no place for a per-range outcome.

This PR introduces a transfer backend the connector talks to, and a TENT implementation of it. TENT settles one task at a time on its own progress thread and can cancel what it started, which the connector can use without changing how it schedules blocks.

No open PR adds a TENT backend to this connector.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR continues [#49462](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49462),
co-authored by me, @SangChengC (who opened it), and @wendadawen, rebased onto
current main.

Adds `cuda_ipc_pool`, a persistent CUDA IPC pool that sends GPU-preprocessed
multimodal features to TP workers over D2D / P2P without a host round trip.
Unlike `torch_shm`, it supports TP > 1.

For an EPD encoder with TP > 1, `direct_rpc` was previously the only transport.
`auto` therefore kept preprocessing on CPU; explicitly selecting GPU still
copied the output back to host. `cuda_ipc_pool` lets `auto` use GPU

items.summary: NPU full-graph replay double-counts the verify block when DSPARK supplies a live CPU KV-length mirror. already publishes in, but the graph replay fallback adds again.

## Motivation

NPU full-graph replay double-counts the verify block when DSPARK supplies a live CPU KV-length mirror. `DsparkTargetVerifier.run_non_compact()` already publishes `prefix_length + verify_width` in `batch.seq_lens_cpu`, but the graph replay fallback adds `captured_req_width` again.

For example, a prefix of 1000 tokens and a verify width of 8 should pass a KV length of 1008 to FIA; replay currently passes 1016. The MLA verify path uses right-aligned causal attention (`sparse_mode=3`), so the incorrect KV length shifts the causal boundary and can expose future candidates and cache

items.title: [Bugfix][CuMem] Retry the host backup copy in wake_up
items.author: fuhefei
items.summary: Fixes CuMemAllocator wake_up to retry host-to-device backup copy after failures instead of leaving allocations with undefined device contents.
items.body:
## Overview

`CuMemAllocator.wake_up()` clears `is_asleep` before copying a host backup back to the device. If that copy fails, the allocation stays mapped with `is_asleep=False` and `cpu_backup_tensor` still set. The next `wake_up()` skips the entry (`if not data.is_asleep: continue`), so the backup is never retried or released and the device contents are undefined.

items.author: xulunfan
items.summary: On SM120/SM121 the DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate indexer cannot start. SM120 passes the indexer's check, so the candidate path is selected, but DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits kernel requires SM100, so is false and raises before the server reaches readiness.
items.body:
Prerequisite for #47210 (SM120/SM121 dense FP8 native block32 DeepGEMM): without this change DeepSeek-V4.1 does not reach readiness on SM12x with either GEMM backend. The two PRs have zero file overlap and no code dependency in either direction.

DeepGEMM's paged **sparse** MQA logits kernel requires SM100, so

before the server reaches readine

items.title: [Fix] parser: Resolve reasoning end markers to their token ids
items.author: furionw
items.summary: Reasoning detectors build by encoding the end marker's text, and keeps a request's grammar off until the generated ids match that sequence. When the tokenizer does not parse special tokens out of text, a special added marker such as gpt-oss's encodes to ordina…
items.body:
Fixes #47205

## Motivation

Reasoning detectors build `think_end_ids` by encoding the end marker's text, and `ReasonerGrammarObject` keeps a request's grammar off until the generated ids match that sequence. When the tokenizer does not parse special tokens out of text (`split_special_tokens=True`), a special added marker such as gpt-oss's `<|end|>` encodes to ordinary ids the model never generates. The gate never opens, so `require_reasoning` requests (structured output, forced tool calls) run without their grammar and nothing reports it. Resolving the marker by id in the shared detector path

items.title: [TRTLLM-17122][feat] Support owner-only MLA KV writes for Helix prefill
items.author: zhaoyuanh-nvidia
items.summary: Helix MLA context-parallel ranks process the prompt for attention, but each rank owns only part of the persistent KV cache. Persist only the compressed KV records assigned to the rank's cache pages while preserving the temporary K/V needed for context attentio…
items.body:
## Description

Helix MLA context-parallel ranks process the prompt for attention, but each rank owns only part of the persistent KV cache. Persist only the compressed KV records assigned to the rank's cache pages while preserving the temporary K/V needed for context attention.

Build a batch-local map from global token positions to rank-local cache slots and pass it through an optional MLA RoPE/append input. Negative slots suppress persistent KV and scale writes without skipping temporary Q/K preparation. Existing callers that omit this input retain their behavior.

Batch-invariant inference at TP=2 reduces the sequence-parallel partials with a symmetric-memory pull kernel instead of an NCCL reduce-scatter. The result is bitwise NCCL's, which is what training uses, and each decode step is about 0.3 ms faster.

items.author: bvolpato
items.summary: With an empty last-failed cache, the wrapper's retry executes the entire passing workload again. A successful rerun can then hide the process failure.
items.body:
## Description

**Motivation.** A parallel unittest process can exit unsuccessfully after its tests pass. With an empty last-failed cache, the wrapper's `--lf` retry executes the entire passing workload again. A successful rerun can then hide the process failure. This wastes test execution and makes the CI result unreliable.

**Change.** Give each parallel attempt and its serial retry a private pytest cache, and set `--lfnf=none`. Pytest teardown removes the cache.

## Description

A chat request whose history replays an assistant turn with tool calls can reach a disaggregated worker without those tool calls.

- **A retry loses them.** OpenAI declares an assistant message's `tool_calls` as an `Iterable`, which pydantic validates into a single-use `ValidatorIterator`. The disaggregated orchestrator serializes the request each time it sends it to a worker (`OpenAIHttpClient._post_with_retry`), and the first serialization consumes the iterator: the resend after a failed attempt carries `tool_calls: []`, and the worker renders the turn without its tool calls.

@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Makes the TRTLLM lowering of the non-causal windowed DSpark draft block cheap. This matters most when acceptance is fixed and only the per-step cost shows.

Why: since efa53ad417, the TRTLLM backend serves a non-causal windowed draft layer as the causal windowed trtllm-gen decode plus a log-sum-exp merge of the block keys after each query (`dflash_merge_future_block_attention`). The merge ran eagerly: dozens of small kernels per layer. On GB300 it cost 61-148 us per layer on top of a 7-94 us decode; the MiniMax-M3.1 drafter runs it in 5 layers every step.

# What does this PR do?
Megatron-FSDP backward-prefetch fix: stop counting buckets that need no all-gather against the prefetch size.

**Prefetch size.** `_extend_by_prefetch_size` counted every bucket toward `suggested_AG_prefetch_size`, including buckets that are not sharded on the gathering group and need no all-gather. ## Description

Adds KV-pressure handling for aggregated Helix: when prefill or decode can't get enough KV pages, the scheduler recompute-pauses (preempts) a request identically on every CP rank and re-runs its prefill later. With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

### What does this PR do?

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

### What does this PR do?

Fix `NIXLCheckpointEngine.build_topology` for a topology with one rollout worker.

instead of no successor metadata and causing `build_process_group` to fail:

    AssertionError: rollout_kwargs[next_agent_metadata] must have length of 1

Use an index relative to `len(metadata)` instead. Topologies with two or more
rollout workers retain the same slice bounds.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.title: fix(rm_hub): accept numeric zero ground truth in grade_answer_verl
items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

### What does this PR do?

Megatron's `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` turns the optimizer into a **HybridDeviceOptimizer (HDO)**: it permanently splits optimizer state between CPU memory and GPU memory via `optimizer_offload_fraction`. …he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

get_rollout_vocab_mask(rollout_name, tokenizer, processor), in workers/rollout/utils.py, is now the single definition

items.author: yph22

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.author: sdc17
items.summary: Nothing errors out and the loss still goes down, so it is easy to miss, but every CP > 1 run that goes through this code path has been training on wrong gradients since #1748. How wrong: - real layer (fla kernels, bf16), CP=4: the input gradient is off by 9.4%…
items.body:
**Right now, with context parallelism (CP > 1), the linear-attention layers send wrong gradients back to the rest of the network.** This hits the Gated DeltaNet layers of Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next, which go through `HuggingfaceAttention` and make up 3 of every 4 layers in these models. items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Description

### 1. Colocate weight sync fails on every GPU but 0 (ROCm)

On ROCm a HIP IPC handle carries the **exporter's** device ordinal, and `hipIpcOpenMemHandle`
resolves it in the **importer's** enumeration; CUDA honours the importer's current device instead.
In colocate mode the trainer exports and the rollout engine imports, so a trainer rank that sees the
whole node exports at ordinal N while an engine launched with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<one gpu>`
enumerates one device where ordinal N does not exist. The two agree only when N is 0 — hence weight

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Summary

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

was parsed as:

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

## Problem

In non-colocated full NCCL weight updates with pipeline-parallel training and multiple independent SGLang rollout engines, each PP source creates a custom `slime-pp_<rank>` group containing itself and every engine GPU.

The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

- Reuse the existing `_wrap_ipv6` helpe

## Summary

Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend.

This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated weight updates with vLLM's native `/update_weights` lifecycle.

- Use  `NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine` on Ascend to send colocated weights.
- Route native `update_info` payloads through `VLLMEngine.update_weights` and vLLM's `/update_weights` endpoint.
- Initialize the native weight transfer engine once

items.title: [Bugfix][Training] Avoid entropy grad graph when entropy_coef is zero
items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

## What

Fix the bundled vLLM `/abort_requests` endpoint in `docker/patch/latest/vllm.patch` so that **abort-all actually aborts**, and add a **cu13 Docker image variant** (partial port of #307).

items.body:
Fixes #312

## Summary
During our own usage, we found that batched Reward Model return values were not validated before assignment; this PR adds return-value validation so malformed batched RM outputs fail before rewards are written.

## Root Cause
The rollout code assigned batched rewards with . When a custom batched RM returned too few rewards, later samples kept ; when it returned too many rewards, the extra values were silently dropped. Also, blindly calling  could convert a top-level , , or  result into keys, characters, or integers whose length happened to match the sample count.
